channel.title: Alerts RSS Feed
channel.description: The RSS Feed for the Alerts page

item.title: Litigation-Related Update: Sileiri Doe Class Members May Request Reopening or Reconsideration of an Adverse Decision Without a Fee
item.description: On Sept. 28, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts issued an order requiring DHS to remediate certain adverse consequences for the class of aliens paroled into the United States after scheduling an appointment through the CBP One mobile app, and whose parole was terminated by the federal government via mass email in April 2025. Sileiri Doe v. DHS, 1:25-cv-12245-ADB (D. Mass).
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Opens Asylum Office in Charlotte
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) is opening an asylum office in Charlotte, North Carolina.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Announces FY 2027 Inflation Increase for Certain Immigration-Related Fees
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services has issued a Federal Register notice that will increase certain H.R. 1 immigration-related fees for fiscal year 2027.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Adjusts EB-5 Fees to Cover Program Costs and Strengthen Integrity Measures
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) is updating fees for the EB-5 Immigrant Investor Program to ensure EB-5 fees fully recover the cost of operating the program, meet statutory processing time goals, and support integrity measures such as audits and site visits.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Reaches H-2B Cap for First Half of FY 2027
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services received enough petitions to meet the congressionally established H-2B cap for the first half of fiscal year (FY) 2027.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: DHS Announces Rule for Certain Children Born in the United States to Foreign Government Employees
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security today issued an interim final rule amending its regulations to allow certain children born in the United States to foreign government employees who are not U.S. citizens to register as lawful permanent residents.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Court Order on Diversity Immigrant Visa Program Hold Policy
item.description: On Aug. 28, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California issued an order in Medani, et al., v. Trump, et al., 26-cv-6332 (NDCA), temporarily vacating PM-602-0193 pending further litigation. USCIS is ordered, “to the extent practicable and in good faith, to take all reasonable steps during the remainder of the Diversity Visa fiscal year to resume ordinary adjudication of plaintiffs’ pending adjustment of status applications without applying” PM-602-0193.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Opens New International Field Office in Ethiopia to Support Fraud Prevention
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) is opening a new international field office in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. The office will begin operations on September 9, 2026, and will handle USCIS immigration matters in Ethiopia.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Recent Court Order on Hold Policies
item.description: On Aug. 24, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California issued an order in Red Eagle Law, L.C., et al., v. Joseph B. Edlow, 26-cv-04850-CRB (NDCA), enjoining PM 602-0192, and PM 602-0194.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS to Publish New Edition of Form I-485; Older Editions Will Be Rejected Starting Sept. 18
item.description: On Sept. 18, 2026, USCIS will publish a revised edition of Form I-485, Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status (edition date: 09/18/26).
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Issues Guidance on Making Public Charge Inadmissibility Determination
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) is issuing updated guidance in the USCIS Policy Manual explaining how the agency will determine whether an alien applying for adjustment of status to that of a lawful permanent resident is likely at any time to become a public charge.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS To Require Electronic Filing of Forms: Strengthening National Security
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is introducing an interim final rule (IFR) that allows U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) to mandate electronic filing, or e-filing, for certain immigration forms.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS to Reduce Frivolous Immigration Benefits Requests by Reinforcing Evidence Standards
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) is clarifying that benefit requestors should establish eligibility for an immigration benefit at the time they file a benefit request.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Reaches Fiscal Year 2027 H-1B Cap
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services has received enough petitions to reach the congressionally mandated 65,000 H-1B visa regular cap and the 20,000 H-1B visa U.S. advanced degree exemption, known as the master’s cap, for fiscal year 2027.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Opens Asylum Office in Atlanta
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) is opening an asylum office in Atlanta. Beginning July 8, 2026, the Atlanta Asylum Office will conduct interviews for affirmative asylum applicants at three locations.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Important Notice for Clients of Former Immigration Attorney Alexandra Lozano
item.description: On May 26, 2026, Alexandra Lozano resigned from the State Bar of Washington in lieu of discipline and is permanently barred from practicing law in Washington.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Court Order on Hold Policies
item.description: On June 5, 2026, the U.S. District Court for the District of Rhode Island issued an order in Dorcas International Institute of Rhode Island, et al. v. United States Citizenship and Immigration Services, et al., 26-cv-00132-JJM-PAS (D.RI.), vacating PM 602-0192, PM 602-0194, and PA 2025-26.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Opens Asylum Office in San Antonio
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services opened an additional asylum office location in San Antonio, Texas. Beginning May 28, 2026, aliens who filed for asylum with USCIS who reside in the jurisdiction of the Houston Asylum Office may be interviewed at either the Houston Asylum Office or the San Antonio Asylum Office.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: DHS Automatically Extends Temporary Protected Status for Lebanon
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security posted a Federal Register notice on the six-month automatic extension of Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Lebanon, from May 28, 2026, through Nov. 27, 2026. Under the TPS statute, if the secretary of homeland security does not decide whether a country still qualifies for TPS at least 60 days before the country’s TPS designation expires, its TPS designation is automatically extended for six months.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Cap Reached for Second Allocation of Returning Worker H-2B Visas for Fiscal Year 2026
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services received enough petitions to reach the cap for the additional 27,736 H-2B visas made available for the second allocation of returning workers for fiscal year 2026 with start dates from April 1 to April 30, 2026, under the H-2B supplemental cap temporary final rule (fiscal year 2026 TFR).
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: FY 2027 H-1B Initial Registration Selection Process Completed
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services has received enough electronic registrations for unique beneficiaries during the initial registration period to reach the fiscal year 2027 H-1B numerical allocations (known as the H-1B cap), including the advanced degree exemption (master’s cap).
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Update on USCIS’ Strengthened Screening and Vetting
item.description: Since taking office, President Trump has prioritized national security and public safety by implementing a series of executive orders and proclamations that mandate strict screening and vetting of foreign nationals seeking entry or immigration benefits.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Reaches H-2B Cap for Second Half of FY 2026 and Filing Dates Now Available for Supplemental Visa Allocations
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services has received enough petitions to meet the H-2B statutory cap for the second half of fiscal year 2026.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: DHS Terminates Temporary Protected Status for Yemen
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security has posted a Federal Register notice regarding the termination of Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Yemen.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Cap Reached for First Allocation of Returning Worker H-2B Visas FY 2026
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services received enough petitions to reach the cap for the additional 18,490 H-2B visas made available for the first allocation of returning workers of fiscal year 2026 with start dates from Jan. 1 to March 31, 2026, under the H-2B supplemental cap temporary final rule (FY 2026 TFR).
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: FY 2027 H-1B Cap Initial Registration Period Opens on March 4
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services announced that the initial registration period for the fiscal year (FY) 2027 H-1B cap will open at noon Eastern on March 4 and run through noon Eastern on March 19, 2026.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS to Increase Premium Processing Fees
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is publishing a final rule that will increase USCIS fees for premium processing to reflect the amount of inflation from June 2023 through June 2025.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: DHS, DOJ Announce Rule to Bar Asylum for Aliens Who Pose Security Threats and Public Health Risks
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) today announced a Federal Register notice that clarifies when aliens may be ineligible for asylum or withholding of removal because they pose a danger to the security of the United States due to certain public health emergencies.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Restores Integrity to the VAWA Domestic Abuse Program After Finding Rampant Fraud
item.description: We are updating guidance in Volume 3 of the USCIS Policy Manual related to the Violence Against Women Act (VAWA) program—a program where certain immigration benefits can be provided to survivors of domestic abuse.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Clarifies Requirements for Professional Athletes
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) today issued policy guidance in Volume 6 of the USCIS Policy Manual to address the U.S. Department of Labor’s (DOL) adoption of the Foreign Labor Application Gateway (FLAG) system, and its effect on certain immigrant visa petitions filed on behalf of professional athletes.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: New Photo Policy Helps Prevent Immigration Fraud Through Enhanced Identity Verification
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) is issuing new guidance that limits the age of foreign nationals’ photos that can be used to create immigration documents to no more than three years. This update enhances national security and prevents identity fraud.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: DHS Ends the Abuse of the Humanitarian Parole Process and Terminates Family Reunification Parole Programs
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security is terminating all categorical family reunification parole (FRP) programs for aliens from Colombia, Cuba, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Haiti, and Honduras, and their immediate family members.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Updates Policy on Biometrics for Detainees
item.description: We are updating USCIS Policy Manual Volume 1, Part C to deter the filing of frivolous claims and provide operational consistency.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: DHS Terminates Temporary Protected Status for Haiti
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security today posted a Federal Register notice on the termination of Temporary Protected Status for Haiti.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Announces FY 2026 Inflation Increase for Certain Immigration-Related Fees
item.description: We have issued a Federal Register notice that will increase certain H.R. 1 immigration-related fees for fiscal year (FY) 2026.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Court Order on Partial Stay of DHS 2024 USCIS Fee Rule
item.description: On Nov. 12, 2025, the United States District Court for the District of Colorado issued a decision in Moody v. Noem, No. 24-cv-00762-CNS (D. Colo.), staying certain EB-5 related fees that were codified by DHS in the 2024 Fee Rule, which became effective April 1, 2024.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: DHS Terminates Designation of South Sudan for Temporary Protected Status
item.description: DHS today posted a Federal Register notice announcing the termination of South Sudan’s designation for Temporary Protected Status.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Presidential Proclamation on Restriction on Entry of Certain Nonimmigrant Workers
item.description: On September 19, 2025, the President issued a Proclamation, Restriction on Entry of Certain Nonimmigrant Workers, an important initial step to reform the H-1B nonimmigrant visa program.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Implements New Immigration Parole Fee Required by H.R. 1
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security is publishing a Federal Register notice to implement a new immigration parole fee required by the H.R. 1 Reconciliation Bill.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Updates Guidance on Military Naturalization
item.description: We are issuing guidance to explain that uncharacterized discharges that occurred on or after Aug. 1, 2024, do not meet the requirement of a separation “under honorable conditions” for former alien service members to naturalize under Sections 328 and 329 of the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA).
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: H-1B FAQ
item.description: On Friday, Sept. 19, 2025, President Donald J. Trump signed a Proclamation, "Restriction on Entry of Certain Nonimmigrant Workers," that took an important, initial, and incremental step to reform the H-1B visa program to curb abuses and protect American workers.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Reaches H-2B Cap for First Half of Fiscal Year 2026
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services has received enough petitions to meet the congressionally established H-2B cap for the first half of fiscal year 2026. Sept. 12 was the final receipt date for new cap-subject H-2B worker petitions requesting an employment start date before April 1, 2026.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: DHS Terminates 2021 Designation of Venezuela for Temporary Protected Status - Sept. 05, 2025
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security today posted a Federal Register notice on the termination of the 2021 designation of Venezuela for Temporary Protected Status.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS to Enforce Consequences for Aliens Who Falsify Information
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services is restoring robust screening and vetting processes to detect aliens seeking to defraud or abuse the immigration system, including aliens who make false claims to U.S. citizenship.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Updates Policy on CSPA Age Calculation
item.description: We are updating the Policy Manual to clarify that a visa becomes available for the purposes of Child Status Protection Act age calculation based on the Final Action Dates chart of the Department of State Visa Bulletin.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Issues Guidance Regarding Family-Based Immigration Policy
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services is issuing policy guidance in the USCIS Policy Manual that will enhance our capability to screen and vet family-based immigrant visa petitions.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Updates Fees Based on H.R. 1
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services is publishing a federal register notice (FRN) based on the H.R 1 Reconciliation Bill (H.R. 1).
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Reaches Fiscal Year 2026 H-1B Cap
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services has received enough petitions to reach the congressionally mandated 65,000 H-1B visa regular cap and the 20,000 H-1B visa U.S. advanced degree exemption, known as the master’s cap, for fiscal year 2026.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: New Fees for Certain Immigration Benefit Requests
item.description: USCIS will soon begin to collect new fees for certain immigration benefit requests. We will provide details on the implementation of these fee changes in the coming days.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Updates Guidance on Validity of Alien Refugee and Asylee Marriages
item.description: We are updating guidance in the USCIS Policy Manual, Volume 4, on valid marriages between a principal asylee or principal refugee and their claimed spouse. Under the updated guidance, all marriages between principal asylees or principal refugees and their claimed derivative spouses must be legally valid under the law of the jurisdiction where the marriage was celebrated in order to be considered valid for immigration benefit purposes.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Update to Policy on Disability Exceptions to Naturalization Requirements
item.description: Under this guidance, USCIS is changing how we process Form N-648 by focusing greater attention on the veracity of medical certifications and identification and prevention of fraud, thereby enhancing the integrity of the process. Across the country and over the decades, there have been numerous instances where the medical certification process has been exploited.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Issues Guidance Regarding Disclosure of Derogatory Information
item.description: States that, if we plan to rely on derogatory information that a benefit requestor is unaware of, we will generally provide a detailed description of the derogatory information in a Notice of Intent to Deny, Request for Evidence, or Notice of Intent to Revoke; and Clarifies when we may not disclose information, such as information that may be classified, sensitive, privileged, or otherwise subject to statutory protections and in other limited circumstances, such as when the information is provided in a third-party record or is subject to disclosure limitations.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Changes Validity Period for Any Form I-693 Signed on or after Nov. 1, 2023
item.description: We are updating Volume 8 of the USCIS Policy Manual to clarify that a Form I-693, Report of Immigration Medical Examination and Vaccination Record, signed by a civil surgeon on or after Nov. 1, 2023, is only valid while the application the Form I-693 was submitted with is pending. If the application a Form I-693 was submitted with is withdrawn or denied, that Form I-693 is no longer valid. This guidance is effective immediately and applies to applications pending or filed on or after June 11, 2025.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Litigation-Related Update: Supreme Court stay of CHNV Preliminary Injunction
item.description: On May 30, 2025, the Supreme Court of the United States issued an order lifting the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts’s April 14, 2025 Preliminary Injunction that stayed parts of the March 25, 2025 Federal Register notice titled, “Termination of Parole Process for Cubans, Haitians, Nicaraguans, and Venezuelans (CHNV).
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: DHS Terminates Temporary Protected Status for Nepal
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security today posted a Federal Register notice on the termination of Temporary Protected Status for Nepal. After reviewing country conditions and consulting with the appropriate interagency partners, Secretary of Homeland Security Kristi Noem determined that conditions in Nepal no longer meet the statutory requirements for TPS.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: DHS Terminates Temporary Protected Status for Cameroon
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security posted a Federal Register notice on the termination of Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Cameroon. After reviewing country conditions and consulting with the appropriate interagency partners, Secretary of Homeland Security Kristi Noem determined that conditions in Cameroon no longer meet the statutory requirements for Temporary Protected Status.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Cap Reached for Additional Returning Worker H-2B Visas for the Early Second Half of FY 2025
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services has received enough petitions to reach the cap for the additional 19,000 H-2B visas made available for returning workers for the early second half of fiscal year (FY) 2025 with start dates from April 1 to May 14, 2025, under the H-2B supplemental cap temporary final rule (FY 2025 TFR).
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Announces Employment Authorization Document Application Procedures for Certain Hong Kong Residents Covered by Deferred Enforced Departure
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services today posted a Federal Register notice for public inspection establishing procedures for certain Hong Kong residents covered by Deferred Enforced Departure (DED) to apply for Employment Authorization Documents (EADs) that will be valid through Feb. 5, 2027.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: FY 2026 H-1B Initial Registration Selection Process Completed
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services has received enough electronic registrations for unique beneficiaries during the initial registration period to reach the fiscal year (FY) 2026 H-1B numerical allocations (H-1B cap), including the advanced degree exemption (master’s cap).
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Reaches H-2B Cap for Second Half of FY 2025 and Filing Dates Now Available for Supplemental Visas
item.description: USCIS received enough petitions to meet the H-2B statutory cap for the second half of fiscal year 2025. The filing dates for supplemental H-2B visas for the remainder of FY 2025 are now available.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Probationary Reinstatements
item.description: The U.S. District Court for the District of Maryland issued a Temporary Restraining Order in Maryland, et al v. United States Dep’t of Agriculture, et al, No. 25-cv-00748, Docket No. 43 (D. Md.) on March 13, 2025.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Update on TPS for Haiti
item.description: On Feb. 20, 2025, Secretary of Homeland Security Kristi Noem partially vacated the July 1, 2024, notice that extended and redesignated Haiti for Temporary Protected Status (TPS).
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Tools Outage
item.description: USCIS will conduct system maintenance to the Contact Relationship Interface System (CRIS) on Wednesday, Feb. 19, 2025 at 11:50 p.m. through Thursday, Feb. 20, 2025 at 2:00 a.m. Eastern.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: FY 2026 H-1B Cap Initial Registration Period Opens on March 7
item.description: Today, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) announced that the initial registration period for the fiscal year 2026 H-1B cap will open at noon Eastern on March 7 and run through noon Eastern on March 24, 2025.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: DHS Terminates the 2023 Designation of Venezuela for Temporary Protected Status
item.description: After reviewing country conditions and consulting with the appropriate U.S. government agencies, Secretary of Homeland Security Kristi Noem has determined that conditions in Venezuela no longer support the 2023 designation of Venezuela for Temporary Protected Status (TPS).
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Update on Form I-134A
item.description: Due to the Jan. 20, 2025 Executive Order, Securing Our Borders, USCIS is pausing acceptance of Form I-134A, Online Request to be a Supporter and Declaration of Financial Support, until we review all categorical parole processes as required by that order.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Waives COVID-19 Vaccination Requirement for Adjustment of Status Applicants
item.description: Effective Jan. 22, 2025, USCIS is waiving any and all requirements that applicants for adjustment of status to that of a lawful permanent resident present documentation on their Form I-693, Report of Immigration Medical Examination and Vaccination Record, that they received the COVID-19 vaccination.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: H-1B Final Rule, H-2 Final Rule, and Revised Form I-129 Effective Jan. 17, 2025
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security’s H-1B final rule and H-2 final rule take effect on Friday, January 17, 2025, modernizing and improving requirements for the H-1B nonimmigrant and H-2 nonimmigrant visa programs.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Updates Guidance on EB-2 National Interest Waiver Petitions
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services is updating its policy guidance to clarify how we evaluate eligibility for the second preference employment-based (EB-2) classification for immigrant petitions filed with a request for a national interest waiver (NIW).
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Updates Filing Procedures for Form I-140
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services today announced a Federal Register notice (FRN) providing updated procedures for submitting a Form I-140, Immigrant Petition for Alien Workers, accompanied by a permanent labor certification, application for Schedule A designation, or national interest waiver (NIW) request.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Cap Reached for Additional Returning Worker H-2B Visas for the First Half of FY 2025
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services has received enough petitions to reach the cap for the additional 20,716 H-2B visas made available for returning workers for the first half of fiscal year 2025 with start dates on or before March 31, 2025, under the H-2B supplemental cap temporary final rule (FY 2025 TFR).
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Offices Closed Jan. 9, 2025
item.description: President Biden has declared Thursday, Jan. 9, a National Day of Mourning to remember the life and legacy of James Earl Carter Jr., the 39th president of the United States, and has issued an Executive Order Providing for the Closing of Executive Departments and Agencies of the Federal Government on January 9, 2025.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS to Publish Revised Form I-129, Petition for a Nonimmigrant Worker
item.description: On Jan. 17, 2025, we will publish a revised edition of Form I-129, Petition for a Nonimmigrant Worker (edition date: 01/17/25). The form has been revised to align with the recently announced H-1B modernization final rule and the H-2 modernization final rule.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Updates Guidance on Flexibilities Available During and After Emergencies or Unforeseen Circumstances
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services is updating our Policy Manual to clarify flexibilities that may be available to benefit requestors during and after an emergency or unforeseen circumstance.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Updates Guidance on Case Assistance and Feedback
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services today announced that it is updating Volume 1, Part A, of the USCIS Policy Manual to reflect the available avenues for case assistance or feedback.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: DHS Publishes Final Rule for the Application of Certain Mandatory Bars in Fear Screenings
item.description: As part of our continued efforts to deliver more timely consequences for noncitizens encountered who do not have a legal basis to remain in the United States—efforts that have resulted in a 60% decrease in unlawful entries since June 4—the Department of Homeland Security has finalized the rule for the Application of Certain Mandatory Bars in Fear Screenings, following publication of the Notice of Proposed Rulemaking in May 2024.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Issues Updated Guidance on Evidence for Applicants Under the International Entrepreneur Rule
item.description: We are issuing updated policy guidance on the types of evidence that may support an application under the International Entrepreneur Rule.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Revised Form I-485, Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status
item.description: On Dec. 10, 2024, we published a new edition of Form I-485, Application to Register Permanent Resident or Adjust Status, which includes updates to questions and instructions. Starting Feb. 10, 2025, we will accept only the 10/24/24 edition of Form I-485 and will reject any older editions of Form I-485.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Reaches Fiscal Year 2025 H-1B Cap
item.description: USCIS has received enough petitions to reach the congressionally mandated 65,000 H-1B visa regular cap and the 20,000 H-1B visa U.S. advanced degree exemption, known as the master’s cap, for fiscal year (FY) 2025.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Now Requires Report of Immigration Medical Examination and Vaccination Record to be Submitted with Form I-485 for Certain Applicants
item.description: We now require certain applicants filing Form I-485, Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status, to submit Form I-693, Report of Immigration Medical Examination and Vaccination Record, with their Form I-485 or the Form I-485 may otherwise be rejected.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: DHS Announces Countries Eligible for H-2A and H-2B Visa Programs
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), in consultation with the Department of State (State), has announced the lists of countries whose nationals are eligible to participate in the H-2A and H-2B visa programs for the next 12 months.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Updates Guidance on Lawful Admission for Permanent Residence Requirement for Naturalization
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services is issuing policy guidance in the USCIS Policy Manual to clarify that a naturalization applicant’s burden to demonstrate they have been lawfully admitted for permanent residence applies only to their initial admission as a lawful permanent resident (LPR) or adjustment to LPR status.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Immigration Medical Examination Documentation Will Be Valid Indefinitely for Certain Afghan Nationals
item.description: We are updating guidance in the USCIS Policy Manual, Volume 8, Part B, Chapter 3, to reflect that immigration medical examination documentation for certain Afghan nationals who arrived in the United States during Operation Allies Welcome (OAW) is valid indefinitely.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Updates Policy Manual Guidance for T Visa
item.description: We are revising our guidance in the USCIS Policy Manual to align with the Classification for Victims of Severe Forms of Trafficking in Persons; Eligibility for “T” Nonimmigrant Status Final Rule.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Updates Guidance on the International Entrepreneur Rule
item.description: We have updated guidance on the International Entrepreneur Rule in our Policy Manual to clarify the required triennial increase in investment, revenue, and other thresholds, and to clarify how we arrange biometrics appointments for certain applicants.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Issues New Guidance on EB-1 Eligibility Criteria for Individuals with Extraordinary Ability
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services is issuing policy guidance in our Policy Manual to further clarify the types of evidence that we may evaluate to determine eligibility for extraordinary ability (E11) EB-1 immigrant visa classifications.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Makes Additional Updates to Policy Guidance for the “Sought to Acquire” Requirement Under the Child Status Protection Act
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services is updating guidance in the Policy Manual (Volume 7, Part A, Chapter 7), to clarify how to calculate the Child Status Protection Act (CSPA) age for noncitizens who demonstrate extraordinary circumstances.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Guidance on Paying Fees and Completing Information for Form I-140, Immigrant Petition for Alien Workers
item.description: Be sure to provide the correct payment and complete information when filing Form I-140, Immigrant Petition for Alien Workers.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Reaches H-2B Cap for First Half of Fiscal Year 2025
item.description: We have received enough petitions to reach the congressionally mandated cap on H-2B visas for temporary nonagricultural workers for the first half of fiscal year 2025. Sept. 18 was the final receipt date for new cap-subject H-2B worker petitions requesting an employment start date before April 1, 2025.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Extends Green Card Validity Extension to 36 Months for Green Card Renewals
item.description: Effective Sept. 10, 2024, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services automatically extended the validity of Permanent Resident Cards (also known as Green Cards) to 36 months for lawful permanent residents who file Form I-90, Application to Replace Permanent Resident Card.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: California Service Center Relocates
item.description: On Aug. 12, the California Service Center (CSC) moved to a new facility as USCIS centralizes processing for immigration benefits.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Updates Guidance for F/M Nonimmigrant Student Classification
item.description: We are updating guidance in the USCIS Policy Manual regarding when students may be eligible for optional practical training (OPT) extensions for Science, Technology, Engineering, and Mathematics (STEM) fields.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: California Service Center Moving to New Address August 12
item.description: On Aug. 12, the California Service Center will move to a new address. The new facility will help streamline processes by concentrating operations in the new location.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Second Random Selection from Previously Submitted Registrations Complete for FY 2025 H-1B Regular Cap
item.description: USCIS recently announced that we would need to select additional registrations for unique beneficiaries to reach the fiscal year 2025 H-1B regular cap numerical allocation.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Will Conduct Second Random Selection for Regular Cap from Previously Submitted FY 2025 H-1B Cap Registrations
item.description: In March, USCIS conducted an initial random selection on properly submitted electronic registrations for the fiscal year 2025 H-1B cap, including for beneficiaries eligible for the advanced degree exemption.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS to Begin Triennial Investment and Revenue Threshold Updates for International Entrepreneur Rule
item.description: Effective Oct. 1, 2024, we will increase the investment and revenue thresholds under the International Entrepreneur Rule, as required every three years. The application fee will not change, however.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Issues Policy Guidance on Children’s Acquisition of Citizenship
item.description: USCIS is updating guidance in the USCIS Policy Manual regarding provisions for children’s acquisition of citizenship.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Reminders on the Process to Promote the Unity and Stability of Families
item.description: On June 18, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) announced actions to promote family unity in the immigration process. This announcement is consistent with the Biden-Harris administration’s commitment to keep families together. DHS is establishing a process to consider, on a case-by-case basis, requests for parole in place from certain noncitizen spouses of U.S. citizens who have been in the U.S. for at least a decade.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: New Policy Guidance on Noncompliance with EB-5 Regional Center Program
item.description: We are issuing policy guidance on new provisions in the Immigration and Nationality Act (INA) that cover consequences for noncompliance with the EB-5 Regional Center program.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Updates Customer Service and Safe Address Procedures for Individuals Protected Under Confidentiality Provisions
item.description: We have implemented provisions in the USCIS Policy Manual that provide guidance on customer service and safe address procedures for individuals protected under 8 U.S.C. 1367.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Extends Employment Authorization Documents under Temporary Protected Status Designations of El Salvador, Honduras, Nepal, Nicaragua, and Sudan
item.description: We are extending the validity of certain Employment Authorization Documents (EADs) issued to Temporary Protected Status (TPS) beneficiaries under the designations of El Salvador, Honduras, Nepal, Nicaragua and Sudan through March 9, 2025.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Clarifies Guidance About How to Adopt a Child under the Hague Adoption Convention
item.description: Effective June 14, 2024, we have updated the USCIS Policy Manual, Volume 5, Part D, to clarify how prospective adoptive parents can adopt a child under the Hague Adoption Convention.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Issues Policy Guidance on Customer Service and Confidentiality Protections for Certain Naturalized U.S. Citizens
item.description: USCIS is issuing  guidance in the USCIS Policy Manual that interprets that the confidentiality protections under 8 U.S.C. 1367 end at naturalization, which will allow naturalized U.S. citizens previously protected under 8 U.S.C. 1367 (specifically, Violence Against Women Act (VAWA) self-petitioners and those seeking or with approved T and U nonimmigrant status) the ability to fully access e-filing and other customer service tools.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Issues Guidance on In-Person Filing for Certain SIJ Petitioners
item.description: We are updating the USCIS Policy Manual to clarify how certain petitioners for special immigrant juvenile (SIJ) classification (or their representatives) may file Form I-360, Petition for Amerasian, Widower, or Special Immigrant.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Shifts Workload for Form I-730 Following-to-Join Refugee Petitions
item.description: Effective May 6, 2024, all Forms I-730, Refugee/Asylee Relative Petition, filed for following to join refugees (FTJ-R) are being processed at the USCIS International Operations Division rather than the Asylum Vetting Center.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Updates Guidance for Family-Based Immigrant Visas
item.description: Effective May 22, 2024, we are updating guidance in the USCIS Policy Manual on family-based immigrant visa petitions (including Form I-130, Petition for Alien Relative and, in limited situations, family-based Form I-360, Petition for Amerasian, Widow(er), or Special Immigrant), including explaining how we handle correcting approval notice errors, requests for consular processing or adjustment of status on the beneficiary’s behalf, and routing procedures for approved petitions.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Opens Additional San Francisco Asylum Office Location
item.description: USCIS’ San Francisco Asylum Office is opening an additional temporary location in Oakland, California. Effective May 15, 2024, asylum applicants under the jurisdiction of the San Francisco Asylum Office may receive an interview notice to appear at the asylum office located in Oakland instead of San Francisco.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Clarifies Policy on Location of H-3 Training
item.description: We have issued policy guidance in the USCIS Policy Manual clarifying when H-3 nonimmigrants may participate in training provided on the property of an academic or vocational institution.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Centralized Intake Processing of VAWA Self-Petitions and Related Filings at the Nebraska Service Center
item.description: Effective April 1, 2024, we centralized the intake process of Form I-360, Petition for Amerasian, Widow(er), or Special Immigrant, and related filings under the Violence Against Women Act (VAWA) for self-petitioning abused spouses, children, and parents at the Nebraska Service Center.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Reminds Certain Employment-Based Petitioners to Submit the Correct Required Fees
item.description: We are updating our Frequently Asked Questions on the USCIS Fee Rule to help certain employment-based petitioners understand how to submit the correct required fees.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Cap Reached for Additional Returning Worker H-2B Visas for the Early Second Half of FY 2024
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services has received enough petitions to reach the cap for the additional 19,000 H-2B visas made available for returning workers for the early second half of fiscal year (FY) 2024 with start dates from April 1 to May 14, 2024, under the H-2B supplemental cap temporary final rule (FY 2024 TFR).
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Adopts Department of Labor Definition of “Science or Art”
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services is issuing policy guidance in the USCIS Policy Manual to add the U.S. Department of Labor (DOL) definition of “science or art” for Schedule A, Group II cases.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Announces Information Regarding EB-5 Regional Center Audits
item.description: Under the new provisions of section 203(b)(5)(E)(vii) added by the EB-5 Reform and Integrity Act of 2022 (RIA) to the Immigration and Nationality Act, we must audit each designated regional center at least once every five years.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Announces New Guidance on Form I-693 Validity Period
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services today announced that any Form I-693, Report of Immigration Medical Examination and Vaccination Record, that was properly completed and signed by a civil surgeon on or after Nov. 1, 2023, does not expire and can be used indefinitely as evidence to show that the applicant is not inadmissible on health-related grounds.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Notice of FY 2025 H-1B Cap Initial Registration Selection Process Completion and Cap Season Reminders
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services has received enough electronic registrations for unique beneficiaries during the initial registration period to reach the fiscal year (FY) 2025 H-1B numerical allocations (H-1B cap), including the advanced degree exemption (master’s cap).
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Revises Policy Manual to Align with New Fee Rule
item.description: We are revising our guidance in the USCIS Policy Manual to align with the Fee Schedule and Changes to Certain Other Immigration Benefit Request Requirements Final Rule published in the Federal Register on Jan. 31, 2024, and effective on April 1, 2024.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Announces Filing Location Change for Certain Employment-Based I-485 and Related Forms
item.description: On, April 1, 2024, U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services is changing the filing location for concurrently filed Forms I-907, Request for Premium Processing Service; I-140, Immigrant Petition for Alien Worker; and I-485, Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status, and for related Forms I-131, Application for Travel Document; I-765, Application for Employment Authorization; and I-824, Application for Action on an Approved Application or Petition, filed with the application package, from USCIS service centers to a USCIS lockbox.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: New Citizens Will Be Able to Seamlessly Request Social Security Updates
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services today announced that, starting April 1, applicants filing Form N-400, Application for Naturalization, will have the option to request an original or replacement Social Security number (SSN) or card and update their immigration status with the Social Security Administration (SSA) without having to visit an SSA office.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: H-1B Form I-129 Filing Location Change and FY 2025 H-1B Cap Season Updates and Reminders
item.description: The initial registration period for the FY 2025 H-1B cap season closed at noon Eastern on March 25, 2024.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Extends Initial Registration Period for FY 2025 H-1B Cap
item.description: USCIS has extended the initial registration period for the fiscal year (FY) 2025 H-1B cap.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Updates Policy Guidance Clarifying Expedite Requests
item.description: USCIS is updating guidance in the USCIS Policy Manual to clarify how we consider expedite requests related to government interests and requests related to emergencies or urgent humanitarian situations, including travel-related requests.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Clarifies Anti-Discrimination Policy
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services today announced agency-wide anti-discrimination guidance that addresses public-facing interactions and affirms our public service principles.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Reaches H-2B Cap for Second Half of FY 2024 and Announces Filing Dates for the Second Half of FY 2024 Supplemental Visas
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services has received enough petitions to meet the H-2B cap for the second half of fiscal year (FY) 2024 and is announcing the filing dates for supplemental H-2B visas for the reminder of FY 2024 made available under the FY 2024 H-2B supplemental visa temporary final rule.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Reminder: Certain Updated Forms Take Effect on April 1 with No Grace Period
item.description: With the new fee rule that goes into effect April 1, 2024, you must use the new 04/01/24 editions
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: FY 2025 H-1B Registration Period and myUSCIS Organizational Account Reminders
item.description: On Feb. 28, 2024, we launched new myUSCIS organizational accounts that will allow multiple people within an organization, as well as their legal representatives, to collaborate on and prepare H-1B registrations, H-1B petitions, and any associated Form I-907, Request for Premium Processing Service. A new organizational account is required to participate in the H-1B Electronic Registration Process starting in March 2024.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Eligible Ukrainians Can Now Apply for Re-Parole
item.description: Beginning Feb. 27, 2024, eligible Ukrainian citizens and their immediate family members who are physically present in the United States can now be considered for re-parole so they can continue to temporarily remain in the United States.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Eligible Ukrainians Can Now Apply for Re-Parole - Russian
item.description: С 27 февраля 2024 года некоторые категории граждан Украины и их ближайшие родственники, которые физически находятся в Соединенных Штатах, могут подать заявку на повторное получение гуманитарного пароля, чтобы иметь возможность временно оставаться в Соединенных Штатах.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Eligible Ukrainians Can Now Apply for Re-Parole - Ukrianian
item.description: Починаючи з 27 лютого 2024 року, певні категорії громадян України та їхніх найближчих родичів, які фізично перебувають у Сполучених Штатах, можуть подати заявку про повторне отримання гуманітарного паролю, щоб мати можливість тимчасово залишатись в Сполучених Штатах.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Changes Fee Payment Process for Filing In-Person
item.description: We are starting a new process for most applicants, petitioners, and requestors, and their attorneys and accredited representatives to pay for certain benefit request forms by mail or remotely instead of in person at a field office.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Updates Guidance on Untimely Filed Extension of Stay and Change of Status Requests
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services today announced an update to its Policy Manual providing that USCIS, in our discretion and under certain conditions, may excuse a nonimmigrant’s failure to timely file an extension of stay or change of status request if the delay was due to extraordinary circumstances beyond the control of the applicant or petitioner.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Cap Reached for Additional Returning Worker H-2B Visas for the First Half of FY 2024
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services has received enough petitions to reach the cap for the additional 20,716 H-2B visas made available for returning workers for the first half of fiscal year 2024 with start dates on or before March 31, 2024, under the H-2B supplemental cap temporary final rule (FY 2024 TFR).
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Issues Policy Guidance on “Ability to Pay” Requirement When Adjustment of Status Applicants Change Employers
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services today issued policy guidance on how we analyze an employer’s ability to pay the proffered wage for immigrant petitions in certain first, second, and third preference employment-based immigrant visa classifications, including instances when the sponsored worker is changing employers.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Changes Filing Location for Form I-907 for Pending Form I-140
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services will begin transitioning the filing location for Form I-907, Request for Premium Processing, when filed for a pending Form I-140, Immigrant Petition for Alien Workers, from the service centers to appropriate USCIS lockboxes on Dec. 15.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Reaches Fiscal Year 2024 H-1B Cap
item.description: USCIS has received a sufficient number of petitions needed to reach the congressionally mandated 65,000 H-1B visa regular cap and the 20,000 H-1B visa U.S. advanced degree exemption, known as the master’s cap, for fiscal year (FY) 2024.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Updates Guidance and Clarifies Policy on Family-Based Conditional Permanent Residence
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services is updating guidance on family-based conditional permanent residence in its Policy Manual. The update consolidates and updates guidance on eligibility, filing, and adjudication for Form I-751, Petition to Remove Conditions on Residence.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: Tampa Asylum Office Moving to New Location
item.description: USCIS’ Tampa Asylum Office is moving to a new location.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Expands myProgress to Form I-485 and Form I-821
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services announced today that we are expanding myProgress (formerly known as personalized processing times) to Form I-821, Application for Temporary Protected Status, and Form I-485, Application to Register Permanent Residence or Adjust Status. myProgress will initially only be available for family-based or Afghan special immigrant I-485 applicants.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Changes Filing Location for Form I-907 With Form I-140
item.description: U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services will begin transitioning the filing location for Form I-907, Request for Premium Processing, when filed with Form I-140, Immigrant Petition for Alien Workers, from the service centers to the USCIS lockbox on Nov. 13.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Updates Guidance for Special Immigrant Juvenile Petitions
item.description: Effective immediately, we are updating guidance in the USCIS Policy Manual for adjudicating Special Immigrant Juvenile (SIJ) petitions.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: DHS Announces Countries Eligible for H-2A and H-2B Visa Programs
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS), in consultation with the Department of State (DOS), has announced the lists of countries whose nationals are eligible to participate in the H-2A and H-2B visa programs in the next year.
item.dc:creator: USCIS

item.title: USCIS Potomac Service Center Will No Longer Accept Paper Responses
item.description: As of Aug. 21, 2023, the Potomac Service Center (PSC) has begun to move to a new facility in Camp Springs, MD, and can no longer receive paper responses to correspondence such as Notices of Intent to Deny (NOID), Notices of Intent to Revoke (NOIR), Intents to Deny (ITD), Requests for Evidence (RFE) or supporting documentation for filings currently pending at the PSC.
item.dc:creator: USCIS
